rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Microbes in Human Welfare fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Chemical pesticides and fertilisers pollute and cost energy. The biological alternative uses living microbes: **biocontrol agents** are microbes (or their predators) that kill pests and weeds; **biofertilizers** are microbes that supply plant nutrients, chiefly by fixing atmospheric nitrogen. Both are the backbone of organic farming.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Biocontrol bank: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt toxin kills insect larvae — Bt cotton carries the gene), Trichoderma (fungus vs plant pathogens), ladybird/Aphatelina beetles vs aphids, Baculovirus (insect-specific, harmless to plants/birds/fish).  ·  Trick 2: Merit line: biocontrol is target-specific, no chemical residue, no resistance build-up — the eco advantage over pesticides.

Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example — why Bt cotton works.** The caterpillar bites the leaf; the plant's own cells now carry the *cry* gene from *Bacillus thuringiensis* and produce an inactive protoxin. The insect's alkaline gut juice dissolves it, the toxin is activated, gut cells rupture and the larva dies within days.…  ·  ## 7. (4) Classify biofertilizers: symbiotic (Rhizobium, Frankia, Azolla-Anabaena) vs free-living (Azotobacter) vs fungal (mycorrhiza).…  ·  ## 8. Both are specific, self-renewing and residue-free.…
